title: 2NE1: The Crush Era
description: Hard questions on 2NE1's 2014 Crush era: Come Back Home, Gotta Be You, MTBD, the album's acclaim and the All or Nothing World Tour.

questions.question: Come Back Home takes its title from a 1995 song by which group, as a tribute?
questions.fun_fact: YG founder Yang Hyun-suk was a member of that group. CL confirmed the nod in an interview, while saying the video would go in a different direction.

questions.question: In its first week, Come Back Home placed No. 2 on the Gaon Digital Chart behind which Girls' Generation single?
questions.fun_fact: A week later it climbed to the top and stayed there for two weeks, the ninth and last No. 1 that 2NE1 scored on that chart.

questions.question: The Come Back Home video, set in a near-future city with a virtual paradise, was compared to which 1999 film?
questions.fun_fact: Dee Shin directed the clip, whose production cost was put at about half a million dollars.

questions.question: Which track on Crush is a solo song by the group's leader, CL?
questions.fun_fact: Its Korean title, Menbung, translates as Mental Breakdown, and in 2017 Billboard ranked it No. 2 on its list of the best K-pop deep cuts of the decade so far.

questions.question: The pop art look of the Gotta Be You video mixes Roy Lichtenstein's comics with which artist's Brillo Boxes?
questions.fun_fact: Designer Jeremy Scott worked with the group on the video, which came out in May 2014 to celebrate five years since their debut.

questions.question: Where did Crush land on Billboard's list of the 10 best K-pop albums of 2014?
questions.fun_fact: Rolling Stone also put it sixth among the best pop albums of 2014, the only record by an Asian artist on that list.

questions.question: Crush includes a Korean version of which song that 2NE1 first released as a Japanese single in 2012?
questions.fun_fact: YG moved the album's digital release from February 24 to February 27, 2014, so that it would line up with CL's birthday.

questions.question: Which YG boy group were special guests on the All or Nothing World Tour from Seoul to Jakarta?
questions.fun_fact: The tour began at the SK Olympic Handball Gymnasium in Seoul on March 1, 2014, and grew to 20 concerts across Asia.

questions.question: After the All or Nothing World Tour, 2NE1's next tour came with their 2024 reunion. What was it called?
questions.fun_fact: YG revealed the reunion in July 2024 to mark the group's 15th anniversary, and the tour opened at Seoul's Olympic Hall that October.

questions.question: At the 2014 Melon Music Awards, Come Back Home won the award for which genre?
questions.fun_fact: It was also named Song of the Year for March at the Gaon Chart K-pop Awards, and it won three music show trophies in March 2014.

title: K-pop and Korean Tradition True or False
description: True or false on Korean tradition in K-pop: hanbok in videos and on stage, gugak instruments, Daechwita and songs that borrow from the past.

questions.question: BLACKPINK dance in modified hanbok in their 2020 video for How You Like That.
questions.fun_fact: The Korea Times reported that Rosé's outfit drew on the cheollik, a garment of military officials, and the group also wore hanbok on The Tonight Show.

questions.question: Haegeum, a 2023 single by Agust D, takes its name from a traditional Korean drum.
questions.fun_fact: A haegeum is a two-stringed fiddle, and the song uses one in its arrangement. The title also works as wordplay on liberation, a theme of the track.

questions.question: Seo Taiji and Boys' 1993 hit Anyhow Song (Hayeoga) features the taepyeongso, a traditional Korean instrument.
questions.fun_fact: Kim Duk-soo is credited with the taepyeongso and samul nori parts, and the album Seo Taiji and Boys II sold over 2.2 million copies.

questions.question: VIXX's 2017 single Shangri-La pairs synths with melodies inspired by Japanese enka.
questions.fun_fact: Its melodies take their cue from gugak, traditional Korean music, and the visuals of the release put Korean tradition front and center.

questions.question: The video for Agust D's Daechwita is based on the 2005 film The King and the Clown.
questions.fun_fact: It draws on the 2012 film Masquerade instead, and Agust D plays both a king and the double who takes his place.

questions.question: NewJeans performed in hanbok at Gyeongbok Palace in Seoul in May 2024.
questions.fun_fact: The show was 2024 Korea On Stage, co-hosted by the Korea Heritage Service and KBS, and a filmed clip showed them singing Cool With You at Geunjeongjeon Hall.

questions.question: Agust D's 2020 song Daechwita samples the traditional Korean military music it is named after.
questions.fun_fact: He has said the idea of using a real daechwita grew into pansori-style storytelling and kkwaenggwari percussion on the track.

questions.question: Billboard described Sunmi's 2019 single Lalalay as Eurodance blended with traditional Korean sounds.
questions.fun_fact: Billboard heard Latin pop and dancehall in it, plus the taepyeongso, a traditional Korean horn. Sunmi shares the production credit with Frants.

questions.question: On Mnet's Queendom in 2019, Oh My Girl covered Lovelyz's Destiny in an arrangement featuring the gayageum.
questions.fun_fact: According to The Korea Times, the choreography of that stage was also styled after the graceful look of traditional Korean art.

questions.question: In her 2021 video for Lalisa, BLACKPINK's Lisa sits on a throne in an outfit modeled on Korean royal court dress.
questions.fun_fact: That look is Thai instead, with a rad klao yod, a pointed headdress mostly seen in Thai traditional dance, and Phanom Rung Historical Park also features in the clip.

title: P1Harmony: From Siren to Sad Song
description: From their 2020 debut with Siren to Sad Song: P1Harmony's name, fandom, leader, singles, a world tour and Billboard 200 entries.

questions.question: Siren was the lead single of P1Harmony's October 2020 debut EP. What was that EP called?
questions.fun_fact: All six members helped write the lyrics of its opening track, Intro; Breakthrough, and the EP reached No. 5 on the Gaon Album Chart.

questions.question: The name P1Harmony joins the word harmony with which two ideas?
questions.fun_fact: The members are meant to add up to one group with endless possibilities for harmonies, and the name is often shortened to P1H.

questions.question: What is the official name of P1Harmony's fandom?
questions.fun_fact: Revealed on April 20, 2021, the name says that fans are the pieces P1Harmony could not do without.

questions.question: Which member is the leader of P1Harmony?
questions.fun_fact: Keeho is also one of the group's vocalists. The six members are Keeho, Theo, Jiung, Intak, Soul and Jongseob.

questions.question: Which single led Disharmony: Break Out, the EP of P1Harmony's first comeback in April 2021?
questions.fun_fact: The EP went on to be nominated for Album of the Year at the 2021 Mnet Asian Music Awards.

questions.question: On which US talk show did P1Harmony make their American TV debut, performing Back Down in November 2022?
options: The Late Late Show with James Corden
The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon
questions.fun_fact: The performance aired on November 29, one day before Back Down came out as the lead single of the EP Harmony: Set In.

questions.question: Which EP, led by Jump, gave P1Harmony their first entry on the Billboard 200 in June 2023?
questions.fun_fact: It entered at No. 51 and sold more than 250,000 copies, double their previous release, while the group placed No. 35 on the Artist 100.

questions.question: With Killin' It, P1Harmony won their first music show trophy in February 2024. On which show?
questions.fun_fact: Killin' It, released on February 5, 2024, was the group's first full-length album and reached No. 39 on the Billboard 200.

questions.question: Where did P1Harmony's September 2024 EP Sad Song peak on the Billboard 200?
questions.fun_fact: The EP tells a story of getting over loneliness through a superhero concept, and it reached No. 2 on the Circle Album Chart.

questions.question: How many cities did P1Harmony's 2023 tour, P1ustage H: P1oneer, visit around the world?
questions.fun_fact: The tour opened on January 14, 2023, and FNC Entertainment counts 40 shows across those cities.

title: Who Directed These K-pop Music Videos?
description: Ten famous K-pop music videos, from Gangnam Style to Ditto: name the director or production company behind each one.

questions.question: Which production company made the 2017 video for the remix of BTS's Mic Drop with Steve Aoki?
questions.fun_fact: Woogie Kim of GDW directed it, and the mic drop at the end of the clip was inspired by Barack Obama's at his last White House Correspondents' Dinner.

questions.question: Which production team directed TWICE's 2016 video for TT?
questions.fun_fact: Kim Young-jo and Yoo Seung-woo of the team had also made Like Ooh-Ahh and Cheer Up, and the TT video drew over 5 million YouTube views in under a day.

questions.question: Who directed BIGBANG's 2015 video for Bang Bang Bang?
questions.fun_fact: Parris Goebel created the choreography, and she can be spotted in the clip herself.

questions.question: Who directed the 2012 video for PSY's Gangnam Style?
questions.fun_fact: The video was shot in Seoul over 48 hours in July 2012, and the same director went on to make the clip for PSY's next single, Gentleman.

questions.question: Which studio made LOONA's 2019 video for Butterfly?
questions.fun_fact: Digipedi stands for Digital Pedicure, and the studio was started by two art directors, Seong Won-mo and Park Sang-woo.

questions.question: Which production team directed (G)I-DLE's 2020 video for Oh My God?
questions.fun_fact: Yoon Rima and Jang Dongju of Rigend Film directed it, and it became the group's third video to pass 100 million views.

questions.question: Who directed the two-part video for NewJeans's Ditto in December 2022?
questions.fun_fact: He is an advertising director who heads Dolphiners Films, and part of the song's lyrics came from Oohyo and The Black Skirts.

questions.question: Which production company made Super Junior's 2011 video for Mr. Simple?
questions.fun_fact: Director Hong Won-ki set it up in 2002 with cameraman Kim Jun-hong, and in 2020 it made the web series Goedam, which Netflix acquired.

questions.question: Which production company made ENHYPEN's 2020 debut video, Given-Taken?
questions.fun_fact: The company's name began as a nickname a college professor gave its founder, taken from a German insult.

questions.question: Who directed Taeyeon's 2016 video for 11:11?
questions.fun_fact: He works with ST-WT Productions, and in 2022 he also directed the video for Girls' Generation's Forever 1.

title: K-pop Song Titles That Ask a Question
description: Easy questions on K-pop songs whose titles ask a question, from What Is Love? and Why Not? to What Do I Call You.

questions.question: Which girl group released What Is Love? in April 2018?
questions.fun_fact: J.Y. Park wrote and composed the song, and it debuted at No. 1 on the Gaon Digital Chart.

questions.question: Which girl group released Why Not? in October 2020?
questions.fun_fact: It led their EP [12:00], and its video shows the members dancing on the surface of the Moon.

questions.question: Which American rapper features on MONSTA X's 2019 single Who Do U Love?
questions.fun_fact: It climbed to No. 26 on Billboard's Mainstream Top 40 airplay chart, the group's first single to enter it, and was up for Best K-pop at the 2019 MTV VMAs.

questions.question: Which BIGBANG member released the solo single Who You? in September 2013?
questions.fun_fact: It came out on September 2, 2013, the same day as Black, a single that features Jennie, then a YG trainee.

questions.question: Which girl group released What's Your Name? in April 2013?
questions.fun_fact: Produced by Brave Brothers, it reached No. 1 on the Gaon chart and is introduced on its EP by a short track called What's My Name?

questions.question: Which soloist released How's This? in August 2016?
questions.fun_fact: She co-wrote the hip-hop and trap track, and its club party video featured one hundred dancers.

questions.question: Which singer released What Do I Call You, her fourth Korean EP and its title track, in December 2020?
questions.fun_fact: The physical edition of the EP also includes Happy, the digital single she had put out in May 2020.

questions.question: Who released the single What You Waiting For in July 2020?
questions.fun_fact: Teddy and R.Tee were among its producers, and in the video she plays several versions of herself, from timid to confident.

questions.question: Who released What Are You Up To as the lead single of his debut EP, Color on Me, in 2019?
questions.fun_fact: Music Bank handed him his first music show trophy as a solo artist for this song on August 9, 2019.

questions.question: Which singer made her solo debut with Why Don't You Know, featuring rapper Nucksal, in June 2017?
questions.fun_fact: The tropical house track is about a love that goes unanswered, and its video shows her dancing across a wide grassy field.
